content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm currently using [product_name] [article_no] with Ethernet to manage pumps and blowers for wastewater purification at reedbed sites. I'm interested in enabling remote monitoring and control, either via [product_name] engineering software or an Android app. Although Ethernet makes this feasible, it can be challenging to ask clients for external LAN access or configure port forwarding to [product_name]. Additionally, since many connections use DHCP, there's often no static IP. I'm therefore considering using a GPRS modem connected to the Ethernet port for remote access over the mobile network. Has anyone tried this? Is it possible? Can you recommend reliable GPRS modems for this task? Also, how is the IP address managed for remote access using the engineering software and Android app?

Hi, It may be possible using the IMO-1 device from [company_name]. You can visit [url] and check out the IMO-1. It's also worth contacting [company_name] to confirm if your requirements can be met with this hardware. As far as I know, they offer a separate VPN network and remote control system, which might be a suitable solution for you. Hope this helps.

From what I understand, the IMO-1 communicates with [product_name] using a serial connection, so it only supports older versions like [article_no] and lower. I need a solution that provides Ethernet connectivity to [product_name].

Hi, I've heard that the IMO-1 is based on the MOROS from [company_name]. The IMO-1 actually has an Ethernet interface, but I'm unsure if it supports communication with [product_name] [article_no]. It's best to confirm this directly with [company_name] for an accurate answer. Hope this helps.

Hi, I'm using an IMO1 for monitoring a [product_name] [article_no] and it works for monitoring via Quirex [product_name] MONITOR, but not for changing network input values. It doesn't work with the [product_name] app, so I'll try your suggested port forwarding solution (forwarding 10001 to PC). You may find more info in this post: [url]

Hi [user_name], You might want to consider a GPRS router from Moxa. It comes with Ethernet support and built-in routing features. We're planning to use it with [product_name] [version_no] for a TCP/IP connection to a third-party server via GPRS. Moxa ON Cell 5104 – HSPA Modem with external antenna and cable. Cheers.

Thank you all for your suggestions! Since I'm seeking a budget-friendly solution—the industrial modems are often more expensive than [product_name] itself—I'm considering trying out a Raspberry Pi. I'll update you on the results as I proceed.

Hi [user_name], I just saw your post. Have you found a solution? I have several animal feed bins at different sites and am thinking of using an ifm laser sensor paired with a [product_name]. If online monitoring is possible, it would be a significant benefit. Kind regards, [user_name]

I'm actively working on this and things appear promising. I connected a basic G3 dongle to the USB port of a Raspberry Pi and successfully accessed the internet over the mobile network. My next step is to set up the Raspberry Pi as an SMS gateway for sending and receiving SMS messages. By the way, this goes beyond the original forum topic—using a Raspberry Pi, there's no need for [product_name] at all, since the Pi serves as a Linux PC and relay boards are available.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking for reliable remote monitoring and control of [product_name] [article_no] in situations where Ethernet-based remote access is complicated by factors like dynamic IP addresses and strict client LAN policies. The built-in Ethernet solution is seen as limiting. Community members are exploring options such as GPRS modems and other third-party routers, but face challenges with hardware compatibility and limitations of available monitoring apps, particularly regarding write access. Cost-conscious users are willing to adopt other platforms (like Raspberry Pi) when solutions based on [company_name] hardware or compatible third-party products are too expensive or restrictive.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward, remote access to [product_name] [article_no] from outside local networks using affordable, easily deployable hardware with Ethernet support. Ideally, solutions should enable both monitoring and control (read and write) via mobile networks.
